title: United States Patent No. 139,121 — 'Improvement in Fastening Pocket-Openings'
creator: Jacob W. Davis, assignor to himself and Levi Strauss & Company
our_rights_determination: Public domain (United States government document, 1873). Title, patentee, dates and the opening of the specification transcribed verbatim from the patent text; we cite the document and reproduce only this short excerpt of its text, not a facsimile image.
gloss: The spotlight document: the 1873 patent that created the riveted blue jean. Titled 'Improvement in Fastening Pocket-Openings', granted 20 May 1873 on an application filed 9 August 1872, to 'Jacob W. Davis, of Reno, Nevada, assignor to himself and Levi Strauss & Company, of San Francisco, California.' Its specification opens: 'My invention relates to a fastening for pocket-openings, whereby the sewed seams are prevented from ripping.'

title: Levi Strauss
creator: Wikipedia
gloss: Source: born Löb Strauß on 26 February 1829 in Buttenheim, in the Kingdom of Bavaria; emigrated to the United States in 1847; the riveted-trousers patent is U.S. Patent 139,121 (1873); died 26 September 1902 in San Francisco.

title: Levi Strauss (biography)
creator: House of Bavarian History (Haus der Bayerischen Geschichte)
gloss: Source for immigration and philanthropy: original name Löb; born 26 February 1829 in Buttenheim; emigrated with his mother and sisters via Bremerhaven in 1847 after his father's death; joined his brothers' New York textiles business and became a United States citizen in 1853; went to San Francisco during the gold rush; a founding member and from 1877 treasurer of the San Francisco Chamber of Commerce; endowed scholarships at the University of California and supported Jewish charities; died 26 September 1902.
